header:
Date: 2028-07-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Evan Martin (Redwood AE), Nina Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Rios (Verdant - Head of ML), Carlos Dominguez (Verdant - Platform Eng), Priya Sharma (Verdant - CTO)
Recording: Zoom
Agenda: high-level integration options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), SDK/langchain support, gateway/proxy and rate limit handling, observability hooks
transcript:
[00:00] Evan: Hi everybody, thanks for joining. I'm Evan from Redwood, AE on this account. Nina and I will run through integration options and answer questions.
[00:08] Maya: Hey Evan, thanks. I, I guess quick context   Verdant runs ML infra for a set of vertical analytics products, we evaluate LLMs for report summarization and insights. We're exploring whether Redwood hosted is ok or if we need Dedicated or Private.
[00:22] Evan: Great, that's exactly what we'll cover. Nina, want to start with SDK + LangChain support?
[00:26] Nina: Sure. Redwood has first-class SDKs for Python and Node, and example repos for LangChain and LlamaIndex. Sorry, I sometimes say LongChain in my notes, ha. We also provide direct REST endpoints and websocket streaming. Most teams use the SDK for client-side batching and retry logic.
[00:40] Carlos: Do you have a sample for LangChain memory integrations? Our stack uses LangChain agents + a Pinecone-like vector store.
[00:46] Nina: Yes    that shows how to call Redwood for streaming completions, and a LlamaIndex example for local retrieval-augmented workflows. The repo includes how to set up prefix/KV cache hints and token estimation. I'll share the link after the call.
[01:02] Priya: Are those examples production-ready or more like quickstarts?
[01:06] Nina: They're intermediate  good for POC and can be hardened for production. They include retry/backoff, idempotency keys, and recommended rate-limit handling patterns.
[01:15] Maya: Speaking of rate limits, our architects worry about throttling at peak. We run about 150 RPS of moderate-length prompts during business hours and spikes to ~400 RPS a few times a day. Latency target p95 under 800ms. Can Redwood meet that?
[01:32] Evan: For Hosted, we have shared pools with soft quotas  for steady 150 RPS you should be fine, but spikes to 400 could hit throttles unless you use Dedicated. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput.
[01:44] Nina: Right. For Dedicated you can define throughput targets and autoscaling policies; also burst capacity is configurable. We can show expected token/sec and concurrency numbers based on your prompt length.
[01:54] Carlos: And Private? If we go VPC/private, how does network egress work do we still use Redwood control plane?
[02:01] Evan: Private deployments can be VPC-peered or fully on-prem. With VPC mode the control plane is a customer-managed control plane option; calls route locally, and audit logs/KMS stay within your network if desired. There is a tradeoff: Private gives full data residency but you'd manage some ops.
[02:15] Priya: Security: SOC 2, ISO, SAML, KMS we need SOC 2 Type II and SAML SSO, plus ability to bring our own KMS.
[02:24] Nina: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestations. SAML SSO and SCIM are supported for RBAC. For encryption, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations in Private and Dedicated; hosted can integrate with KMS for some secrets but you can opt for BYOK in Private. We'll attach the security pack.
[02:40] Maya: Good. Operationally, we need observability per-route latency, token-level cost breakdown, traces that join our system traces, and logs for audits.
[02:49] Evan: That's a core part of Redwood Console you get per-model and per-route dashboards, token/cost split, and tracing hooks. We support OpenTelemetry to ship traces into your tracing backend and can emit logs to your S3 or ELK.
[03:02] Carlos: For the gateway we have an internal API gateway/proxy that handles auth and routing. Can Redwood be used behind our proxy or do you recommend sending requests directly?
[03:11] Nina: Both are supported. Most customers put Redwood behind their gateway for auth and rate-limiting. We also provide a lightweight sidecar/gateway sample that performs request signing and health checks. If you want to do traffic shaping, it's often easiest at your edge gateway and let Redwood handle batching and KV caching on the runtime side.
[03:29] Maya: You mentioned caching how does KV/prefix caching interact with LangChain workflows? We want to avoid recomputing long contexts every call.
[03:36] Nina: The runtime supports KV cache for autoregressive state (for chat) and you can configure prefix cache for static context. For RAG with LangChain/LlamaIndex, we recommend caching retrieved docs and embeddings at your vector store layer and use Redwood's request-level cache for static prompt prefixes. It reduces token costs and latency.
[03:54] Evan: Also, Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization/profile settings if you plan Dedicated on GPUs that reduces unit cost and can improve throughput.
[04:02] Priya: If we do Dedicated, how do rollouts/versions work? We need canary, A/B, and an automatic fallback to hosted if capacity issues arise.
[04:11] Nina: Rollouts are supported you can do canary deploys and route percentages per model version. We also support fallback policies so if Dedicated capacity is exhausted requests can route to a compatible hosted model variant. All policies are configurable in the YAML deployment manifest.
[04:26] Carlos: Any gotchas integrating with LlamaIndex? We use LlamaIndex in a few microservices for chat summarization.
[04:33] Nina: We have an adapter that shows how to plug Redwood as the LLM backend. The most common friction is differences in streaming behavior and token accounting, so we provide a shim that maps stream chunks and a small utility to translate LlamaIndex call patterns to Redwood's SDK.
[04:47] Maya: What's the typical latency profile for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[04:51] Evan: Dedicated on GPU z-high throughput nodes typically hits p95 200-400ms for short prompts (p50 even lower); Hosted is slightly more variable due to multi-tenant scheduling p95 might be 400-900ms depending on model and seq length. We'll need your prompt samples to give more precise numbers.
[05:07] Priya: Pricing ballpark numbers for Dedicated and what commitment looks like?
[05:12] Evan: I can send a dedicated pricing sheet but rough idea: monthly reserved capacity with commit tiers; we also offer a flexible burst layer. Pricing depends on instance family, throughput, and retention/observability add-ons. We'll include a sample cost model.
[05:24] Carlos: For rate limits, we want per-API-key quotas and per-route throttles. Is that supported?
[05:30] Nina: Yes. We support token-level quotas, per-route settings, and per-key rate-limits. You can configure soft limits with grace periods and hard limits that return 429. We also provide meterings so your billing maps to the quotas.
[05:44] Maya: One more compliance: we run some regulated data, so data retention policies and audit logs are critical.
[05:50] Nina: You can set log retention windows and redact logs for PII. In Private/Dedicated you can push logs to your own S3 and we can disable certain storage. Audit trails for each request are available.
[06:01] Evan: Quick technical: if you want to run a LangChain POC, the usual path is: 1) share sample prompts and traffic profile; 2) we provision a short-lived Dedicated trial or host a capacity-limited sandbox; 3) run benchmarks with your prompts including p95/p99 latency and cost per 1k tokens; 4) tune batching/quantization.
[06:18] Maya: That sounds good. For the POC we'd prefer a Dedicated trial to see true throughput.
[06:22] Evan: We can do that. Nina will coordinate the environment and the LangChain/LlamaIndex examples.
[06:27] Priya: Any limitations with our infra we run in GCP with private VPCs and use Cloud KMS.
[06:33] Nina: GCP VPC peering is supported. For Cloud KMS, we can integrate for key wraps in Private deployments. Some small networking config is needed but we have a runbook.
[06:43] Carlos: Can you emit traces with our trace ids so we can join spans?
[06:47] Evan: Yes, OpenTelemetry hooks and we can accept a trace-id header and join traces in Redwood Console.
[06:53] [small crosstalk] Maya: okay good 
[06:56] Evan: Quick recap and next steps: we'll send Dedicated pricing and SLA, attach SOC2/security pack, Nina will share LangChain/LlamaIndex example repo and gateway snippets, and we'll schedule a technical deep-dive the week of 7/19 to run benchmarks.
[07:12] Priya: Perfect. Anything else on your side?
[07:14] Carlos: No, that's it.
[07:16] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[07:18] Evan: Thanks we'll follow up with notes and ship the items.
[07:21] [END]
